promise: A fleet with no AWS in it is a working setup, not a broken one: preflight is not a problem when neither EC2 nor SSM is wanted, a host whose source never reported a state is neither dimmed nor labelled, and it is still asked for its login.
why: Issue #1, from someone whose seven hosts all come from ~/.ssh/config. The setup screen called an empty ~/.aws a fault, every row was dimmed and labelled 'unknown', every host was painted the terminated red because that was the colour an unrecognised state fell through to, the cluster never drew them at all, and the login probe skipped them because it required state == running. Hangar was an EC2 tool first and three of its four sources arrived without the EC2 parts being revisited. Asserts each named case passed by name, not that some line in the output said zero failures: the first draft of this case did that and stayed green with the mistake planted, because a filtered run prints one line per suite and the suite that still passed supplied the zero. Mistake 16, in the case written to guard against it.
command: out=$(scripts/test.sh --filter 'testAFleetWithNoAWSIsNotAProblem|testAWSIsNotUsedWhenNeitherEC2NorSSMIsWanted|testAHostWithNoStateSaysNothingAndIsNotDimmed|testAnImportedHostHasNoStateAtAll|testAHostWithNoStateIsStillAsked' 2>&1) || exit 1; for t in testAFleetWithNoAWSIsNotAProblem testAWSIsNotUsedWhenNeitherEC2NorSSMIsWanted testAHostWithNoStateSaysNothingAndIsNotDimmed testAnImportedHostHasNoStateAtAll testAHostWithNoStateIsStillAsked; do printf %s "$out" | grep -q "$t\]. passed" || exit 1; done
